decision.question: Are the scene's major surfaces represented with pencil-like surface marks or graphite texture?
decision.criteria: Pass if pencil-like surface mark-making is visibly established across major surfaces through fine directional strokes, hatching, form-following marks or convincing deposited graphite texture. Inspect the marks themselves: they must read as drawing material on the depicted surfaces, rather than merely random noise superimposed on photographic texture. Fine strokes and retained color do not disqualify pencil drawing. Fail if substantial surfaces show only photographic material texture, desaturation or undifferentiated grain without convincing pencil-like marks. This condition concerns surface mark-making, not whether the underlying tonal gradients and reflections have also been converted to pencil shading. Use unknown only when the visible evidence cannot establish the character or extent of the marks.

Distinguish drawing-material texture from undifferentiated speckling over photographic surfaces; describing the image as grainy or textured alone does not establish pencil mark-making. Directional hatching is not mandatory when deposited graphite texture is visibly convincing. Assess the marks themselves, not contour strength, color reduction or completion of underlying tonal modeling. Cite visible examples supporting the judgment. Use unknown only if the evidence cannot establish the marks' character or extent, not merely because confidence is low or assessments disagree. The target is pencil-drawn representation of the image's visual content; the reference is the supplied image and the requested pencil-drawing transformation.
